items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023
items.q: we would be on sessions and the saxophones would be Mike Brecker and Ronnie Cuber and Dave Sanborn and myself.

ctx.x: Yeah. I have to say that you and some of your bandmates present challenges to interviewers and here’s why. I’m going to read this from, maybe a publicist wrote this: “Lou Marini is the seasoned soul and adept multi-instrumentalist, arranger, composer, educator and producer credited with inspiring the origins of a fan-following cult across multiple genres of music.” So which thing am I going to ask you about?

You know when I was in school at North Texas State I was a jazz snob. And then I was playing with Les Elgart’s band and we had a gig up in — Les used to pick up, as did many bands — would pick up horn sections from North Texas. So we were playing with all kinds of — I mean I played the Lipizzaner Stallions, I played the Fort Worth Rodeo, I played the little military base gigs in the officers’ club, I mean every possible gig you can imagine. Ice shows, Stevie Wonder, Gladys Knight & the Pips, you know we ran the…

history is so broad is that I like all kinds of music and the challenge of fitting in and trying to be yourself and play something pure and still honor the genre and not go outside of it, which I always thought was a great challenge. That was one of the things about the years in the jingles in New York. You know at ten o’clock in the morning you’re playing flutes with like a Mozart style classical ensemble, and an hour later you’re playing a New Orleans style funk tenor solo on a jingle you know. And I always…
